question:
Assertion (A): If $A$ is a $3 \times 3$ skew-symmetric matrix, then the determinant of $A$ is zero.

Reason (R): The diagonal entries of a skew-symmetric matrix are always zero, and every $3 \times 3$ skew-symmetric matrix has at least two identical rows.
explanation:
The determinant of any odd order skew-symmetric matrix is zero (this is a standard result proven using the properties of determinants).
However, the reason is false because for a $3 \times 3$ skew-symmetric matrix, the diagonal entries are zero, but the matrix need not have two identical rows.
For example:
$A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & a & b \\-a & 0 & c \\-b & -c & 0\end{bmatrix}$ has all unique rows unless $a,b,c$ have special values.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
